parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Separate variables correctly to obtain $\int\frac1{x+2}\,dx=\int\cot(\theta/2)\,d\theta$ [B1]. Guidance: equivalent integrands; integral signs SOI. Obtain $\ln(x+2)$ [B1]. Guidance: modulus signs not needed. Obtain a term of the form $k\ln\sin(\theta/2)$ [M1]. Obtain $2\ln\sin(\theta/2)$ [A1]. Use $x=1$, $\theta=\pi/3$ to evaluate a constant, or as limits, in an expression containing $p\ln(x+2)$ and $q\ln(\sin(\theta/2))$ [M1]. Guidance: reach $C=$ an expression or a decimal value. Obtain the correct solution in any form, e.g. $\ln(x+2)=2\ln\sin(\theta/2)+\ln12$ [A1]. Guidance: $\ln12=2.4849\ldots$; accept constant to at least 3 s.f.; accept with $\ln3-2\ln(1/2)$. Remove logarithms and use the correct double-angle formula [M1]. Guidance: need correct algebraic process; $(x+2)/12=(1-\cos\theta)/2$. Obtain $x=4-6\cos\theta$ [A1]. Total: 8.
